full_title: A Light for Attracting Attention by The Smile
name: A Light for Attracting Attention
name_with_artist: A Light for Attracting Attention (artist: The Smile)
description_preview:
A Light for Attracting Attention is the debut studio album from the rock super-group The Smile. The album has been highly-anticipated since the band’s official live debut at Glastonbury in May 2021, during which a set of eight new songs was presented to the public.

During an interview for Consequence of Sound in July 2021, the longtime Radiohead collaborator and The Smile’s producer, Nigel Godrich revealed that the super-group’s first album was already in the works, describing it as it follows:

[It’s not] a rock record. […] It’s an interesting juxtaposition of things, but it does make sense. It will make sense.

The LP’s lead single, “You Will Never Work In Television Again,” was officially released on January 5, 2022, along with the announcement of three concerts in London for January 29 and 30, 2022: all of the live performances were also streamed online and unveiled new songs, such as “Speech Bubbles” and “The Same”.

Four more singles followed: “The Smoke,” “Skrting on the Surface,” “Pana-vision” and “Free in the Knowledge”.

On April 3, the album’s official title and artwork got leaked on Shazam: the image appeared when users opened the service to scan the track “Pana-vision,” which was featured in the last episode of the sixth season of BBC’s TV show, Peaky Blinders. In addition, the announcement post from a venue for a future The Smile show revealed the release date was set to be May 13.

Finally, on April 20, 2022, the band officially made the album available for pre-order.

body.plain:
Standard Vinyl Back Cover Artwork




The back cover of the vinyl edition of A Light for Attracting Attention features another painting by Stanley Donwood and Thom Yorke, called “Unchecked” (2022).

Like the front cover, the zigzag blue patterns evoke rivers, currents, or contour lines from old maps, but here they’re stretched across almost the entire canvas. The overall composition feels like a “zoomed out” or alternate perspective – still abstract, but suggestive of terrain or water systems.

body.plain:
Rough Trade Exclusive Vinyl Back Cover Artwork




Painting by Thom Yorke and Stanley Donwood

The faded background brushstrokes give a sense of weathering, like an old navigational chart that’s been handled and faded over time. Compared to the standard edition back cover, this one feels less like turbulent waters and more like an arid landscape or a desert map – perhaps thematically complementing different emotional zones of the album. The root-like tendrils and winding rivers suggest connection and branching pathways, a recurring motif in this series of artworks.
